about.title: Bellflower Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Bellflower takes many shapes. Some people spend their shifts in warehouses and auto shops along Alondra Boulevard; others drive delivery routes down Bellflower Boulevard, Clark Avenue, or Woodruff Avenue; still others care for patients, stock shelves, or build homes across this Los Angeles County city of 78,441. Workers' compensation in California generally covers medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who caused the accident, and it is usually the only claim you can bring against your employer. But a separate injury claim may exist when someone outside your company played a role, such as a subcontractor, a property owner, the maker of faulty equipment, or another driver. That last one matters here: Bellflower recorded 357 injury collisions in 2025, with 513 people hurt and 10 lives lost, and many workers are on the road at the Friday evening hours when crashes tend to cluster. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who can look at both pieces of your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Bellflower Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Two Claims, One Conversation
items.desc: Workers' comp is normally your exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker can open a separate claim. An attorney in our network can evaluate both without you paying anything up front.

items.title: Deadlines Kept Straight
items.desc: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and third-party claims carry a two-year filing window. Getting connected early helps keep both clocks in view.

items.title: Protection From Pushback
items.desc: Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim is illegal in California. If your hours were cut or your job was threatened after you spoke up, that is worth raising with an attorney.

items.question: I was hit on Alondra Boulevard while making deliveries for my Bellflower employer. Is that a work injury or a car accident?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were on the clock, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and a portion of lost wages regardless of who was at fault. If the other driver was negligent, you may also have a separate injury claim against that driver, which follows California's two-year deadline. An attorney can help you pursue both without one undercutting the other.

items.question: Can I sue my employer directly for a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: Usually not. Workers' compensation is designed to be the exclusive remedy against your employer, even when the employer was careless. The exceptions are narrow, which is why attorneys often focus on whether an outside party, such as a subcontractor or the manufacturer of defective equipment, contributed to what happened.

items.question: How quickly do I need to report a work injury in Bellflower?
items.answer: California asks you to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury or of learning it was work-related. Reporting in writing and keeping a copy is a simple way to protect yourself. If your employer punishes you for reporting, that retaliation is illegal and can be addressed on its own.
